name: Alsi
actions: Source of fibre and plant omega-3 fat
traditionalUses: Roasted seeds as a mouth freshener
kitchenUse: A tablespoon of freshly ground, roasted seeds stirred into roti dough, curd or a glass of water.

typicalUse.adultAmount: 1–2 tablespoons of ground seeds a day, with plenty of water
typicalUse.note: Grind seeds just before use; whole seeds often pass through undigested.

cautions.note: Medicinal amounts may not be safe in pregnancy; the evidence is unclear, so keep to food amounts.
Little is known about medicinal amounts while breastfeeding.
Avoid with a narrowed or blocked bowel. Take with enough water; large amounts can cause bloating. Do not eat raw or unripe seeds.

interactions.effect: Flaxseed or its oil may add to the effect of blood thinners.
The fibre can slow absorption of medicines; take them an hour before or two hours after.

evidence.summary: Flaxseed may modestly help weight loss in adults with obesity and insulin resistance in gestational diabetes; its effect on other conditions is unclear.
